title: The export

blocks.what_we_do: Identify the relationship between reports and the genotype matrix used for analysis.
blocks.why: The report excerpts show how calls are labelled. The matching BED/BIM/FAM set holds the complete course genotype matrix. BED stores genotypes in binary; BIM describes variants; FAM describes sample order. These three files are a matched set. In module 2 we convert to the PLINK 2 native PGEN/PVAR/PSAM format while checking identity and order.
blocks.you_need: The matched laboratory export from 0.5; concepts from 1.1?1.6.
blocks.command:
```{r s1-7}
initial <- check_bed(cfg$input)
print(initial)
stopifnot(initial$samples == 2016L, initial$variants == 299523L)
```

blocks.expected_result:
2,016 sample wells and 299,523 variants. No QC has yet been applied and no case/control phenotype is present in the initial FAM.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with the supplied simulated dataset.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Can you combine a BED from one release with a FAM from another if their sample counts match?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Equal counts do not establish matching sample identity, ordering or genotypes.

</details>
